The Integration Pitch

Scaling Praana Beyond Point-to-Point Integrations

Aarogya Tech built Praana to close the gap between hospital visits and the health data captured everywhere else — vitals devices, a patient companion app, a provider guide app, and live connections into eClinicalWorks and athenahealth are already in place. As the company moves from pilot clinics toward health-system contracts, the strategic asset isn't any single sensor or app; it's how cleanly Praana's data reaches whatever EHR, lab, or care-management system the next customer already runs.

Every new deployment that needs a bespoke interface to a client's EHR is a sales cycle stretched longer and an engineering team pulled off the product roadmap. For a venture-backed platform company, that's not a technical footnote — it's the difference between growth that scales and growth that gets bottlenecked by integration debt one contract at a time.

Vorro gives Aarogya Tech a single interoperability layer — FHIR, HL7, C-CDA, and REST/webhook connectors — so each new eClinicalWorks, athenahealth, or hospital EHR relationship becomes a configuration exercise, not a custom build. That frees Dr. Thakur's team to compete on what Praana actually does — earlier detection, individualized baselines, fewer avoidable readmissions — while ambient documentation and automated coding sit ready as a natural expansion once the connectivity layer is standardized.
